Multinational Corporations (MNCs), Class 10 Economics, Globalisation and the Indian Economy. One example: design in the US, parts in China, assembly in Mexico and Eastern Europe, service from India.

• An MNC owns or controls production in more than one country
• Why spread out: cheap labour, closeness to markets, resources, favourable government policies
• The goal: lower cost, higher profit (savings sometimes as much as 50–60%)
• Result: production gets interlinked, and MNCs drive globalisation
